solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One struck by particular moment late in game (5,5)

blocks.note: a match is the thing you strike to get a flame
a point is a particular, a single detail, as in 'point by point'

annotation.surface: A player is hit by a ball just as the game reaches its climax.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One struck' reads as a person hit; it is the thing you strike to get a flame.
annotation.definitionFit: It is the stage in tennis when the leading player needs just one more point to win, so it only arrives near the end.

entries.clue: Endlessly call him a vile, terribly conniving person (11)

indicatorNotes.Endlessly: without an end, so the word loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.terribly: the letters are treated terribly, knocked out of order

blocks.note: the rest of the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone vents about a scheming man by calling him vile names.
annotation.walkthrough: Niccolò Machiavelli wrote The Prince, and his name became a byword for cunning, so a capital-M answer can stand for any schemer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Florentine author of The Prince advised rulers to use deceit, and his name is now used of any unscrupulous plotter.

entries.clue: Channel without lead feature (5)

indicatorNotes.without lead: a word's lead is its front letter, and 'without' says to go on without it

blocks.note: a strait is a narrow sea channel
the S at the front is dropped

annotation.surface: A TV channel is missing its main programme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television; here it is water, as in the Strait of Dover.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a distinguishing quality of someone's character.

entries.clue: How a magician may reveal ropes they rearranged (3,6)

indicatorNotes.rearranged: the letters of 'ropes they' are literally arranged again in a new order

annotation.surface: A conjuror's rope trick: the ropes were tangled and now come out restored.
annotation.walkthrough: The ropes fit the magic show perfectly, which hides that they are only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: It is the exclamation a conjuror makes as the trick is unveiled, so it describes the manner of the unveiling.

entries.clue: My friend is former head? (3,4)

blocks.note: old = former, as in 'my old school'

annotation.surface: Someone boasts that their pal used to be a headteacher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former head' looks like an ex-headmaster. The answer is dated upper-class British slang for a chum, the sort of thing P. G. Wodehouse's Bertie Wooster says.
annotation.definitionFit: A jocular old-fashioned British form of address, used where you might say 'my dear chap'.

entries.clue: Lack of cutting implements must put out the last of cafeteria diners (7)

indicators: must put out the last of

indicatorNotes.must put out the last of: to put out is to eject, and what gets ejected is the last letter of 'cafeteria'

blocks.note: no = a lack of, as in 'no money'
the final A of cafeteria is removed from SHEARS

annotation.surface: A canteen has run out of cutlery and has to turn away its last customers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put out the last of cafeteria diners' reads as evicting customers. Nosh is informal British for food.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British: people who nosh, that is eat, are the ones having a meal.

entries.clue: Most of group is featured in performances — they’re musicians! (12)

indicatorNotes.Most of: most but not all, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.featured in: a feature appears within a show, so these letters appear within the performances

blocks.note: used as it stands, after the shortened group
acts = performances; it wraps round the two chunks above, split AC…TS

annotation.surface: A music group's line-up mostly appears in the concerts, and the clue cheers them as musicians.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end after the dash; 'they're musicians' describes the people, so the plural answer fits.
annotation.definitionFit: Players who support a soloist or singer, typically at the piano, are a kind of performer of music.

entries.clue: I’m a chic star, frightfully alluring (11)

indicatorNotes.frightfully: in a frightful state, the letters are thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: A vain celebrity describes themself as stylish and irresistible.
annotation.walkthrough: The boast is the answer in disguise: a chic star would describe themself exactly this way.
annotation.definitionFit: Having a compelling personal magnetism that draws people in.

entries.clue: Looking sulky, having been denied power trip (6)

indicatorNotes.having been denied: to be denied something is to go without it, so the word goes without the P

blocks.note: pouting = pushing out the lips sulkily

annotation.surface: A child sulks after being refused permission to go on an excursion.
annotation.walkthrough: P = power is a standard abbreviation from physics.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short pleasure excursion, a day out.

entries.clue: Bad-tempered piano worker maybe holding another instrument up (8)

indicatorNotes.holding: the piano and worker hold the instrument between them
indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, going up means writing the word bottom to top

blocks.note: a lute is a stringed instrument
a worker is a kind of ant

annotation.surface: A grumpy piano mover struggles while also carrying another instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piano worker' looks like one person, a piano mover; it is P and ANT, and they hold the reversed lute between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sulky and irritable like a child who cannot get their way.

entries.clue: State expanded once stripped of its borders? (5,8)

indicatorNotes.stripped of its borders: a word's borders are its edges, its first and last letters, and these are stripped away
indicatorNotes.expanded: an abbreviation is expanded when it is written out in full

blocks.note: ONCE loses O and E, leaving the two letters NC
NC is a US postal code; its N written out in full
and its C written out in full

annotation.surface: A US state grew larger after once losing territory at its frontiers.
annotation.walkthrough: Borders reads as a state's frontiers; they are just the two end letters of 'once'. Expanding an abbreviation into its full form is an unusual move worth noticing.
annotation.definitionFit: One of the fifty members of the United States, on the Atlantic coast.

entries.clue: Height of king embodied in sculpture (7)

indicatorNotes.embodied in: to be embodied in something is to be given form inside it, so the king goes inside the sculpture

blocks.note: a statue is a sculpture; the R sits just before its last letter

annotation.surface: A statue captures how tall a monarch stood.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about a king's size shown in stone, which is why the definition and wordplay blend so well.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: how tall a person stands, their natural build.

entries.clue: Wanted shoes muddied and made to seem worn (11)

indicatorNotes.muddied: muddied water is stirred up, and so are these letters

annotation.surface: Coveted shoes got muddy and ended up looking old.
annotation.walkthrough: The muddy shoes suit the definition so well that 'muddied' passes for plain description.
annotation.definitionFit: Denim treated this way is tumbled with pumice stones so that new cloth looks faded and old.

entries.clue: Flatmate is unable to accept house being upended slightly (2-8)

indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so the outer word takes in the pieces
indicatorNotes.upended: in a down entry, standing a word on its other end writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: can't = is unable; it opens after its first letter, C…ANT

annotation.surface: A flatmate can't bear the house being turned upside down even a little.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' only joins the two chunks; 'house being upended slightly' reads as one messy house.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who lives under the same roof as you shares the flat, so it is a formal word for a flatmate.

entries.clue: Monster crab dish prepared with thyme in the middle (9)

indicatorNotes.prepared: a dish is prepared by working its ingredients, and these letters are worked into a new order
indicatorNotes.in the middle: only the letter in the middle of 'thyme' goes in

annotation.surface: A recipe: crab cooked with thyme, and the result is monstrous.
annotation.walkthrough: The cooking surface hides a Greek myth: the answer is the whirlpool facing Scylla across the strait Odysseus sailed.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is a sea creature who swallows the water three times a day, making a deadly whirlpool.

entries.clue: Round element making up Bridget Riley work? (2,3)

annotation.surface: A circle is one of the shapes that make up a Bridget Riley painting.
annotation.walkthrough: Bridget Riley is a British painter famous for dizzying black-and-white patterns, the leading name in optical art.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Riley's paintings are the best-known British instance of this optical style.

entries.clue: In two minds, primarily after delaying one’s transport to Oz? (7)

indicatorNotes.primarily: in the first place, so only the first letter of each word is used

blocks.note: first letters of After Delaying One's

annotation.surface: Someone can't decide whether to put off their trip to Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: Oz looks like Australia; it is the land Dorothy reaches in The Wizard of Oz.
annotation.definitionFit: In The Wizard of Oz a twister carries Dorothy's Kansas house away to the magical land.

entries.clue: An elegant interior refurbished over several time periods (17)

indicatorNotes.refurbished: a refurbished room is done up in a new arrangement, and so are these letters

annotation.surface: A stylish room has been redone many times over the years.
annotation.walkthrough: The home-makeover picture makes 'time periods' sound like eras of decor; they are generations.
annotation.definitionFit: It means spanning or involving more than one generation, and a generation is a span of roughly thirty years.

entries.clue: I’m surprised about operation of a restaurant (5)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters are written backwards

annotation.surface: Someone is amazed by the way a restaurant is run.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the adjective in 'house wine' or 'house special': the establishment's own.
annotation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means belonging to the establishment itself, as in the red wine it serves as standard.

entries.clue: Elects to do wrong following various other terrible examples at first (5,2)

indicatorNotes.following: the wrongdoing comes after, following, the initials
indicatorNotes.at first: only what comes first in each word, its initial letter, is taken

blocks.clueFragment: various other terrible examples at first
blocks.note: first letters of Various Other Terrible Examples

annotation.surface: A complaint that a ballot went wrong, following a string of other bad cases.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts SIN after the initials even though the clue gives it first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to choose someone for office by ballot.

entries.clue: Meaningful reference book? (9)

blocks.note: the surface reads this as significant, important; the setter means literally full of meanings
a book you consult rather than read through, and the question mark flags the pun

annotation.walkthrough: 'Meaningful' usually means significant; read it literally as full of meanings, which a book of synonyms is.
annotation.definitionFit: Roget's lists words grouped by sense, so it is a reference work packed with meanings.

entries.clue: Dance in loose-fitting dress (6)

blocks.note: a 1920s dance in which the shoulders and hips shake
an old word for a chemise, a loose shift

annotation.surface: Someone dances wearing a baggy frock.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rarer one: the word began as a corruption of chemise.
annotation.definitionFit: The word names both a jazz-age shaking step and, as a corruption of chemise, a loose shift.

entries.clue: Artist appeared before the crowd, being filmed (2,6)

blocks.note: an actor who is on is performing in front of the audience

annotation.surface: A painter made a public appearance while the cameras rolled.
annotation.walkthrough: The three chunks are assembled in the reverse of their clue order, so reading the clue backwards gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Something in front of a rolling lens is being recorded on film or video.

entries.clue: Fair cut introduced by travel operator (8)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: a guest is introduced by a host who speaks first, so the operator comes first

blocks.note: lanced = cut, as a boil is

annotation.surface: A reasonable price cut offered by a tour company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair cut' looks like a fair price reduction; 'cut' is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a report that weighs both sides evenly is impartial.

entries.clue: Rest of song has to be abridged (3,4)

indicatorNotes.to be abridged: an abridged text is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a Lied is a German art song, as by Schubert
the S at the end goes

annotation.surface: The remainder of a song has to be cut short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like the remainder of the song; it is the verb, to take a break.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to lay yourself flat for a nap or a break.

entries.clue: Precise name given by director? (6)

blocks.note: a sign that directs you the way to go

annotation.surface: A film director supplies an exact name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Director' wants to be a film director; it is a signpost pointer.
annotation.definitionFit: A tight, strictly limited reading of a rule is exact, as in 'in the narrow sense'.

entries.clue: Hot air from mouth on hand (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, one piece placed on another sits after it

blocks.note: give someone a hand = applaud them
trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

annotation.surface: Someone blows warm breath onto their hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is applause, as in 'a big hand for our speaker'.
annotation.definitionFit: Empty talk meant only to win applause is pretentious nonsense, windbaggery.

entries.clue: Trust men to whom money is owed (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition means 'one to whom money is owed'

blocks.note: to credit a story = to believe, trust it
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: Put your faith in the people you owe cash to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Men' as other ranks is army shorthand.
annotation.definitionFit: A lender, or anyone a debt is payable to, is the other side of a debtor.

entries.clue: Soup and a portion of lamb or schnitzel (6)

indicatorNotes.a portion of: a portion is a helping cut from a larger dish, and the answer is cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: runs from the end of lamb into schnitzel

annotation.surface: A menu order: a starter, then some lamb or a schnitzel.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a variant spelling of borscht.
annotation.definitionFit: The beetroot broth of Eastern Europe, also spelt with a final T.

entries.clue: Continue in private, perhaps, certainly not upset (7,2)

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, and in a down entry that turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: a private is one kind of soldier

annotation.surface: Carry on quietly in private, and don't get upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In private' reads as secretly; 'private' is the army rank.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for keeping going doggedly despite difficulty, as a soldier marches on.

entries.clue: In the past, arcades regularly overlooked marketplaces (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
indicatorNotes.overlooked: in a down entry, to overlook is to sit above, so the first chunk is written on top

annotation.surface: Old shopping arcades used to look out over the market squares.
annotation.walkthrough: Arcades and marketplaces share one scene, which hides that 'arcades' is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The open public squares of ancient Greek cities were where trading and assembly happened; this is the Latin-style plural.

entries.clue: Chance of promotion almost restricted by design (11)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word, so the last letter is left off
indicatorNotes.restricted by: to be restricted by something is to be hemmed in by it, so the chunk goes inside

blocks.note: intent = design, purpose; it opens after IN to take the chunk

annotation.surface: A worker's shot at promotion is limited by how things were set up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chance' is an adjective here, as in a chance meeting. 'By design' looks like the definition's opposite; 'design' is INTENT.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective for what happens without intention, accidental, as in 'a chance remark'.

entries.clue: Civic council’s penultimate closure could produce problem that only gets worse (7,6)

indicatorNotes.penultimate: last but one, so the next-to-last letter of 'council' is used
indicatorNotes.could produce: the letters could be worked into something new, rearranged

annotation.surface: A town council shutting a facility for the second-to-last time could start a downward spiral.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penultimate closure' reads as one phrase; 'penultimate' belongs with 'council's' and picks out its I.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a chain of causes in which each trouble feeds the next and the loop keeps deepening.

entries.clue: Cooked fish badly in good wine (11)

indicatorNotes.in: being in something means sitting inside it, so the badly chunk goes inside the wine

blocks.note: the char is a fish of the trout family
red = red wine; it opens after its R

annotation.surface: Some fish was poorly prepared in a fine wine sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooked fish' wants to be one phrase; 'Cooked' is the definition and 'fish' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Grilled over high heat until scorched with dark lines, one particular way of preparing food.

entries.clue: Lists of clubs taken on by awful politicians (11)

indicatorNotes.taken on by: a recruit taken on by a firm joins it, so the C joins the chunks around it

annotation.surface: Membership rolls of golf clubs have been seized by dreadful politicians.
annotation.walkthrough: Tories are British Conservatives.
annotation.definitionFit: Books or databases of names and addresses, such as a telephone book, are catalogues of entries.

entries.clue: Sensible way to go to gain re-entry? (4-2-5)

annotation.definition2: way to go to gain re-entry

blocks.clueFragment: way to go to gain re-entry
blocks.note: a returning spacecraft heads back towards our planet

annotation.surface: A wise way to get back in somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Re-entry' sounds like returning to a building; it is a spacecraft re-entering the atmosphere.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiomatically it describes practical people; literally it is the direction a returning capsule travels.

entries.clue: Oversee excellent plan (11)

blocks.note: to intend = to mean to do

annotation.surface: Supervise a brilliant scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plan' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be in charge of work and watch that it is done properly.

entries.clue: Avatar wearing pink (11)

blocks.note: in = wearing, as in 'dressed in blue'
pinks are the flower family that includes this bloom

annotation.surface: An online character dressed in pink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like the colour; it is the flower.
annotation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a deity's descent in bodily form is its avatar, so the Sanskrit word means embodiment.

entries.clue: Birds periodically surrounded by friendly cow (10)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular periods, so every other letter is taken
indicatorNotes.surrounded by: the letters are surrounded, enclosed, by the next word

blocks.note: intimate = close, friendly; it opens after INTIM

annotation.surface: Birds keep landing around a tame cow in a field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is a verb here, to cow someone, and the farmyard of birds and a friendly cow hides that.
annotation.definitionFit: As a verb, to cow someone is to frighten them into submission.

entries.clue: Faulty indicators containing uranium and corrosive fluid (7,4)

indicatorNotes.Faulty: faulty things are out of order, and so are these letters
indicatorNotes.containing: the letters also contain, take in, the uranium symbol before mixing

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

annotation.surface: Broken gauges have uranium in them and some caustic liquid.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry surface hides that 'indicators' is anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: HNO2 is a weak but reactive acid that exists only in solution, so it is a caustic liquid.

entries.clue: Community organisation’s informal change brought about enlightenment (6)

indicatorNotes.brought about: a ship brought about turns to face the other way, so the letters are written backwards

blocks.note: WI = the Women's Institute, with the 'S
a mod is informal for a modification

annotation.surface: A local group's casual reforms led to a new understanding.
annotation.walkthrough: The WI, Women's Institute, is a British community organisation for women, known for jam and village events.
annotation.definitionFit: Deep understanding and good judgement, the state of being enlightened.

entries.clue: Position on committee with my boss worked out (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, one piece placed on another sits after it

blocks.note: com. is an abbreviation for committee

annotation.surface: A committee role shared with the boss has been settled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Position' reads as a job on the committee; it is the verb, to put.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: calculated, found by arithmetic.

entries.clue: It’s only a snippet, but grabs hold of readers at the start (7)

indicatorNotes.grabs hold of: something grabbed is held inside the grasp, so the letter goes inside
indicatorNotes.at the start: only the start of the word, its first letter, is used

blocks.note: but = except, as in 'all but one'

annotation.surface: A blurb admits it's only a sample, but it hooks readers from the first line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like a joining word in the surface; it is EXCEPT.
annotation.definitionFit: A short passage taken from a longer book or film is a fragment of it.

entries.clue: Make adjustments to old car outside a library (9)

indicatorNotes.outside: the old car stands outside, around, the pieces that follow

blocks.note: a crate is slang for a decrepit old car; it opens after its C
lib. is an abbreviation for library

annotation.surface: Tinker with a banger parked outside a library.
annotation.walkthrough: An old crate is slang for a worn-out car.
annotation.definitionFit: To set an instrument against a standard and correct its readings is to fine-tune it.

entries.clue: Dish ultimately from America found in part of Japan (8)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: in the end, so only the last letter of 'from' is used
indicatorNotes.found in: America is found inside the Japanese city

blocks.note: a Japanese city; it opens after its first letter

annotation.surface: A dish that finally arrived from America turns up in Japan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately from' looks like a phrase about origin; it just picks the M of from.
annotation.definitionFit: A Greek baked meal of layered aubergine, minced lamb and white sauce.

entries.clue: Container of flowers well-kept around public transport station (4-4)

indicatorNotes.around: turned around means facing the other way, so the whole assembly is written backwards

annotation.surface: A neat flower pot is placed around a bus shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal applies to the joined pair, not to each word separately; flower-pot and bus-shelter imagery keeps the transport reading hidden.
annotation.definitionFit: The place on a street where trams halt to let passengers on and off.

entries.clue: Woke up and, in the absence of Charlie, drank freely (7)

indicatorNotes.in the absence of: when Charlie is absent, his letter is missing from the word

blocks.note: to carouse is to drink freely
C = Charlie in the NATO alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: Someone woke up and, with their friend Charlie gone, drank heavily.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a person; it is the radio code word for C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the literal sense: roused from sleep.

entries.clue: Basic formal attire, lacy at the front (6)

indicatorNotes.at the front: only what stands at the front of each word, its first letter, is used

blocks.note: first letters of Attire and Lacy

annotation.surface: A plain, formal outfit with lace at the front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Formal attire' wants to be one phrase, evening wear; 'formal' is PRIM and 'attire' gives only its A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: primary, fundamental, as in a primal instinct.

entries.clue: Record I mostly describe as sound (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word but not all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: CALL (to call something X is to describe it) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A music reviewer calls a recording decent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'sound' suggest music; 'sound' means valid, as in a sound argument.
annotation.definitionFit: An argument that follows correctly from its premises is valid and reasoned.

entries.clue: City in Oregon, Louisiana, North Dakota, and Ohio (7)

blocks.note: O is an old abbreviation for Ohio

annotation.surface: A quiz asks for a place found in four different states.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is in none of them; it is in Florida. The states only lend their abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Florida home of Walt Disney World.

entries.clue: Ham surplus somewhere in Australia (7)

annotation.surface: Too much gammon sent somewhere Down Under.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like meat, and 'surplus' encourages that; it is the verb, to perform too broadly.
annotation.definitionFit: As a verb, to ham it up is to perform with exaggerated gestures and emotion.

entries.clue: Get out ahead of helium blast (6)

indicatorNotes.ahead of: one thing ahead of another comes first, so in a down entry it is written above

blocks.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

annotation.surface: Run before the helium explodes!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blast' reads as an explosion; it is the verb, to attack harshly.
annotation.definitionFit: To attack with withering criticism, the root of 'scathing'.

entries.clue: Ingredient in ramen somewhat often … OK, infrequently! (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: to some extent, so only some of the letters that follow are used

blocks.note: runs from the end of often, through OK, into infrequently

annotation.surface: A cook admits to using some ramen ingredient often, then backtracks: well, rarely.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis and the change of mind are pure surface; the answer runs across the words.
annotation.definitionFit: These thin white Japanese mushrooms are a common topping in noodle soup.

entries.clue: Surgeon screened odd parts of body randomly for skin damage (6,6,5)

indicatorNotes.screened: to screen is to shield, so the surgeon and the other fodder enclose the body letters
indicatorNotes.odd parts of: the odd-numbered letters of the word are taken
indicatorNotes.randomly: at random, so the letters come out in no set order

annotation.surface: A surgeon scans some strange areas of a patient's body looking for skin injuries.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Screened' serves twice: in the surface it is a medical scan, in the wordplay both letters and a hint that the B and D sit among them.
annotation.definitionFit: Burns of this grade go through the outer layer into the dermis, so they are injuries to the skin.

entries.clue: Severely criticise item on a pub menu? (5)

blocks.note: to give someone a grilling or a verbal battering
the Sunday lunch of cooked meat and vegetables

annotation.surface: Pan a dish on the pub's menu.
annotation.walkthrough: A Sunday roast is the traditional British lunch of roast meat and vegetables, served in many pubs.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means both to criticise mercilessly and a joint of oven-cooked meat served as a meal.

entries.clue: Parks possibly filled with fantastic type of redness (7)

indicatorNotes.filled with: a container filled with something holds it inside, so the name holds the next chunk

blocks.note: Rosa Parks, the US civil rights activist; opens before its last letter

annotation.surface: Some parks are full of an amazing kind of red colour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parks' looks like green spaces; it is a surname, so 'possibly' points to a person called Parks.
annotation.definitionFit: A chronic skin condition that causes flushing on the face, so it is a kind of reddening.

entries.clue: River close to port split (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of something is its end, so only the last letter of 'port' is used

annotation.surface: A waterway near a harbour divides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near'; it means the end letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of England's major waterways, flowing through Nottingham to the Humber.

entries.clue: Brief opportunity to catch horse and carriage (9)

indicatorNotes.Brief: something brief is cut short, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.to catch: to catch something is to hold it, so the shortened word holds the horse

blocks.note: CHANCE without its last letter; it opens after CH
an Arab is a breed of horse

annotation.surface: A short-lived chance to grab a horse and cart.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is an old open coach used for British day trips; the word comes from French char à bancs, a carriage with benches.
annotation.definitionFit: Originally a horse-drawn vehicle with rows of benches, later a motor coach for outings.

entries.clue: Secret plan characteristic of Volkswagen and Daimler merger? (6,6)

annotation.definition2: characteristic of Volkswagen and Daimler merger

blocks.clueFragment: characteristic of Volkswagen and Daimler merger
blocks.note: run the two names together and a six-letter word for a list of business sits concealed at the join: volkswAGEN DAimler

annotation.surface: A car-industry merger is suspected of having a secret motive.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half describes itself: run VOLKSWAGEN into DAIMLER and the word AGENDA is literally concealed at the join.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase means a concealed motive, and it literally describes the word for a meeting's list sitting inside the joined names.

entries.clue: A little red buggy, not handled correctly (3-7)

indicatorNotes.buggy: full of bugs, faulty, as software is, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A small red pushchair was not looked after properly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buggy' looks like a pushchair; it means faulty, as in buggy software.
annotation.definitionFit: Abused or mistreated, dealt with cruelly or carelessly.
